retained_skill: Diagnose and repair interacting correctness bugs in a custom PyTorch transformer encoder while preserving its public interface.
bottleneck: All 12 scored attempts recognized positional-encoding and usually attention-scaling defects, but every submitted implementation retained pre-norm encoder layers; the grader requires post-norm although the original instruction only said layer normalization and called the model standard, which does not distinguish two widely used legal conventions.
change: Repair the hidden architectural requirement in the instruction by stating that each encoder sublayer uses post-norm: residual addition first, then layer normalization. This is instruction-level direction at the exact missed decision; it exposes no patch and leaves the student to locate and repair both sublayers plus the other transformer bugs.
restore: Remove the standalone post-norm sentence to restore the original task after the student learns to inspect normalization placement relative to residual paths.
prediction: The change addresses the repeated action of preserving calls such as normalization before self-attention. With the intended ordering stated, some attempts will inspect and move both normalization operations after their residual additions, while still having to diagnose scaling and positional encoding. This prediction is refuted if revised attempts continue submitting pre-norm layers or if all 12 solve without making the remaining debugging decisions.
